html:
The Malyangaba were an Aboriginal Australian people of the dry country on the border between New South Wales and South Australia, north of Broken Hill. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of them. Their land is low hills, stony plains and sand, where water lay in rock holes and creek beds after rain, and people moved between known waters. Neighbours on the map include the Wilyakali, the Bandjigali and the Adnyamathanha. Sheep stations and later mining reached the area in the second half of the 1800s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
